classification.difficultyReason: Distinguishes absence of intersections from absence of solutions by comparing the graphs everywhere.

content.prompt: Bob graphed $y=|x|$ and $y=-1$ and concluded that since they do not intersect, the solution to $|x|>-1$ has no solution. Is he correct?

answer.short: No. The graph of $y=|x|$ is always above $y=-1$, so the solution is $x\in\mathbb{R}$.
answer.worked:
The graph of $y=|x|$ lies on or above the $x$-axis, so it is above $y=-1$ for every real $x$.

Thus $|x|>-1$ holds for all $x\in\mathbb{R}$. Bob is incorrect.

spec.description: Authored graphical comparison of the two functions named in the question.
